requirements.requirement: Repair bin/timeline.py so the supplied events are converted using their explicit numeric UTC offsets and written to timeline.tsv in UTC chronological order while retaining event IDs and messages.
requirements.summary: The repaired script produced the exact expected UTC sequence E1 at 13:00Z, E2 at 13:30Z, and E3 at 14:00Z with IDs and messages retained; the same result was reproduced after restart.

requirements.requirement: Use event ID as the tie-breaker for events representing the same UTC instant.
requirements.summary: A bounded test using three equivalent instants with different offset formats produced A, B, C event-ID ordering.

requirements.requirement: Place invalid timestamps in rejected.tsv without guessing a time zone.
requirements.summary: The supplied invalid E4 record was written unchanged to rejected.tsv, and direct tests showed that a missing offset and an impossible date were rejected.
The east.tsv and west.tsv SHA-256 hashes match the preparation baseline and remained unchanged through implementation and restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained installed. The repaired script executed successfully and passed an in-memory syntax compilation under the installed Python 2.4.3, including after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart result and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, SSH unavailability bounded the disruption, a different post-restart boot ID was observed, and the script, source hashes, outputs, and platform were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot transition.
limitations: The legacy host has no systemd, so the lifecycle collector could not report failed units; no task-specific daemon was involved.
The lifecycle package-health command is unsupported by this old yum version and returned usage text both before and after execution, so package consistency was not directly assessed.

The recorded outcome for cmd-1e47fb4355014de3 is inconsistent with its displayed syntax error, although its command flow indicates the invalid candidate was not installed and later evidence directly validates the corrected script.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Operational hygiene was strong overall. One unnecessary failed implementation mutation created a Python-2.4-incompatible temporary script; it was not installed and was removed before the corrected implementation (cmd-1e47fb4355014de3). The required restart command created /tmp/timeline-reboot.log, which remained afterward as minor executor-caused residue (cmd-d4589efaf02f42e5; global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files). Other mutations directly implemented the repair, generated required outputs, ran bounded edge-case evidence, restored the supplied outputs, or performed the mandatory restart protocol. No new listening sockets or platform changes were observed.
